newsitem.title: USA: Two Florida men charged in AIDS name leak.
newsitem.headline: Two Florida men charged in AIDS name leak.

text.p: Two Florida men have been charged in connection with the leak of a list of the names of 4,000 AIDS patients, the nation's largest breach of AIDS confidentiality, health officials said on Friday.

William B. Calvert III, 35, charged on Thursday with misusing the list, is a former worker with the Pinellas County Health Departmet who was alleged to have used the list, which he carried around in a portable computer, to screen dates for himself.
Calvert's roommate at the time, Gregory S. Wentz, 34, allegedly copied Calvert's information and mailed computer diskettes containing the list to two local newspapers and to the Health Department.
But Dr. Patricia Ryder, director of the Pinellas Health Department's Disease Control Division, said on Friday she did not think the leak of the names had gone any farther.
"We have no reason to believe that anyone's confidentiality has been any further breached," she said. "We believe the Florida Department of Law Enforcement has all the disks in existence."

The case received widespread notice as an example of the risks of the computerization of confidential medical information. Ryder said it had prompted her department to improve its security procedures.

Calvert and Wentz were charged with misdemeanor violations and issued citations to appear in court on March 6. Neither has been jailed. Calvert faces a possible one year in jail and a $1,000 fine, while Wentz could receive 60 days in jail and be fined $500.

"I'm surprised the charge is only a misdemeanor," said Dr. Kathleen Farrell, executive director for the AIDS Community Project of Tampa Bay. "It could have had very serious repercussions for the people on the list. We had a lot of calls from clients panicking because they felt vulnerable."
